title: Web surface
subject: user-organization-mgmt

purpose.intro: The module's frontend lives in `web/` and follows the contribution pattern: the app mounts what the module exports; pages travel inside route definitions and are never imported directly.

claims.text: `UserOrgMgmtProvider` — flat-bag context. Builds the module-owned API client from `UserOrgMgmtWebConfig { apiBaseUrl, authPath?, clientPath? }`; base paths are injected so the SAME code serves a side-by-side test mount (`/api/auth-v2`) and the final mount (`/api/auth`).

`getUserOrgMgmtRoutes()` — `/login`, `/register`, `/forgot-password` + `/reset-password` (recovery split at the sign-in moment), `/my/settings/{account,profile,security,legal}`, `/resolve` (the wizard), `/organizations` (the platform DIRECTORY + `/current` for the active org), `/my/memberships` + `/my/invitations` (linked from the shell's user menu), `/accept-invitation` (?id= capability URL, public — signing in or registering continues on `/my/invitations/accept?id=`, signed in but ungated: accept first, then resolve), the public legal viewer (`/legal-documents?type=`, ?orgTypeId narrows, ?docId pins a version) and the authoring pages (`/manage-legal-documents` + `/:documentType/:orgTypeKey` — under the app's default-gated shell, mirroring the server's `/legal-admin`) as framework-agnostic `RouteDefinition`s (path, page, access, `makeProps`). The app hangs them under its own layouts.
`useSession` / `useInvalidateSession` — react-query session state; query keys live in one catalog (`userOrgMgmtQueryKeys`, `"uom"`-prefixed — a client-side cache namespace, no `-v2` to outlive).

`useActiveMembership` — the caller's membership in the session's active org (`{ organizationId, orgType, roles }` or null), off the session view, no second fetch. The app's nav filters on it: entries naming `requiredRoles` show to a membership holding one of them, inheritance included (the app's `useMemberRoles` expands roles through the access-control forests, `rolesImpliedBy`). Visibility only — the server enforces. In-page controls still render for everyone; sites owed that narrowing carry a greppable `AC(availability-check): <entity>.<action>` marker.
`usePendingInvitationCount` — the caller's pending-invitation count; the shell badges its "My organizations" user-menu entry with it.

`createApiClient` — typed fetch wrappers for every module endpoint; in-module so removing the module breaks consumers at compile time. Every request carries the active org from the module's client-side store (`web/lib/active-org.ts`, localStorage-backed) as the `x-active-organization` header; switching orgs is a store write plus a session-query invalidation, and the OrgSwitcher self-heals an empty or stale store to the first membership.

**The config drives; pages render.** RegisterPage is ONE screen, and every field on it comes from `GET /auth/config` — which identifiers are offered, whether the credential is a password or a delivered code, which profile fields to ask for, which consent items to show. The client invents nothing. LoginPage likewise offers exactly the identifiers and factors the config resolves.

Submitting the form delivers a code and creates NOTHING: every answer — the password included, when the config collects one — stays in component state and rides the verify request, the one that births the account with its address verified and its password set. The code step offers resend (a fresh flow from the held form) and edit-my-details (back to the form); a refresh mid-code just means redoing the form, since nothing exists server-side.
**One component per file.** Pages compose from `web/components/<feature>/` (e.g. `components/register/ConsentCheckboxes`).
**No router hooks in pages.** URL data arrives as props via `makeProps`; navigation goes through the injected `RouterAdapter`.

**Uploads go through the module's own endpoints.** Avatar/logo upload asks the module API for a presigned PUT (`POST /me/profile/avatar-upload`, `POST /organizations/:orgId/logo-upload`); the SERVER derives the storage key from the session/active org — the client never chooses paths, so authorization is intrinsic. The browser PUTs the bytes straight to storage (`web/lib/upload.ts` validates image type + 2MB cap) and the module persists the returned public URL. The avatar saves on pick; the org logo rides the Organization info card on the active-org page — logo + name, one Save. Storage itself is an api-side mount injection (`storage` port), not a web adapter.

**A 428 routes to `/resolve` from anywhere.** The provider builds the client with a gate-blocked hook: any request that lands 428 redirects to `/resolve` carrying the current page as `?intention=` (read via `RouterAdapter.currentPath` — pathname+search). The handler seeds the shared gate query so the screen paints instantly, collapses parallel 428 bursts into one navigation, skips `/resolve` itself so mid-resolution state survives, and admits only in-app intention paths. Omitting the router adapter omits the behavior (headless consumers keep plain thrown errors); `gateCheck()` never fires the hook — it probes.

**Pages are chrome-less.** The hosting app supplies the page frame — the auth card around login/register/recovery, the signed-in shell (sidebar, sign out) around the account pages. Pages only render their own content column.
**Copy speaks to people, not developers.** Page text says "Profile", "Verified", "Signed-in devices" — identifier/credential/session vocabulary stays in code and docs.

reference.statement: `ConsentDecisionList` is the ONE renderer for consent items (see legal.md (`./legal.md`) for the flag semantics table). Its wrappers supply the data: `ConsentCheckboxes` (registration, platform scope), the invitation accept page (`joinConsent` off the public view), and `ReconsentCard` on `/resolve` (the gate's pending-consent projection).
